prompt:
Reference image: the attached picture is the first picture of this series, a digital painting of a harbour at dusk. Use it only as a sample of the painting: match its brush handling, brush texture, soft edges, haze, palette, light and level of detail exactly, as if painted by the same hand on the same day. Do not copy its composition, its layout or its objects: this is a new picture of a different place, described below. The harbour appears only small, seen through the window.

Style: atmospheric digital painting for a 2D side-scrolling adventure game, in the painterly manner of hand-painted 2D platformer and exploration game backgrounds of the 2010s and 2020s. Painted with large soft digital brushes and a few textured brushes: soft edges, visible brush texture, big simplified shapes, little fine detail, no outlines. Strong aerial perspective in clearly separated depth planes: the far distance dissolves into luminous haze, the middle ground has muted, low-contrast values, the nearest objects are darker and more saturated. Thin veils of mist lie between the planes and on the water. The light sources glow warmly. Limited palette: deep teal, slate blue and dusty violet for shadows and distance, warm amber and orange only for the horizon band and the lights. Calm, quiet, slightly melancholic mood. Not a photograph, not a 3D render, not a postcard, not an oil painting with thick impasto, not a cartoon with ink outlines.

Series rules, identical for every picture of this series. Time of day: dusk, as in the harbour picture of this series: outdoors and in the windows the sky is deep teal and slate blue with low clouds, a band of warm orange light at the horizon and the first stars. Light: cool, soft dusk light everywhere; warm amber and orange light comes only from the horizon band and from the lamps, fires and lit windows named below, each with a small warm pool of light on the nearby surfaces; the shadows are deep teal and dusty violet. Composition for a side-scrolling game level: strict side view at eye level, flat horizon at 45 % of the image height (indoors: the horizon seen through the windows), no tilt, no fisheye, no wide-angle distortion, vertical lines stay vertical. Layout for a game screen: the picture will be cropped to a wide 16:9 screen, so the top tenth and the bottom tenth hold nothing important; the floor or the ground where characters walk is an open, uncluttered strip between about 60 and 75 % of the image height; the bottom quarter of the picture is a calm, plain, darker foreground without important objects (a semi-transparent text bar will cover it). The picture is one single still image that will be brought to life with subtle animated layers (drifting mist, moving clouds and water, flickering lights): keep the sky, the water and every light source as clearly separated, readable areas with clean edges.

Location: the parlour of the harbour-master's small stone cottage in Lornholm, a fictional island in a northern sea, at dusk, seen from inside. A low room with whitewashed stone walls and dark wooden ceiling beams. On the left a stone fireplace with a black kettle hanging over the glowing embers. In the middle, against the back wall, a sturdy wooden table with two chairs, a teapot, a candle in a brass holder and a folded sea chart. On the right a small deep-set window shows the dusky harbour and, in the distance, the white lighthouse with its lamp lit; beside it a shelf with a few books, a brass barometer and a model sailing boat, and an oilskin coat on a hook by the door. A braided rag rug on the stone-flag floor.

Leave the floor and the path free of people and animals: it is a game background, characters are added later as separate sprites.

Do not paint effects that the game animates: the fire in the fireplace only as low glowing embers with a soft warm glow, no tall flames, no sparks and no smoke; the candle only as a small soft glowing spot; the distant lighthouse lamp only as a tiny glowing dot without a beam. These effects are animated separately in the game.

No text, letters, numbers, signatures, watermarks or logos anywhere in the image. No real places, brands, franchises or recognisable characters from existing games or films.

Image format: landscape 3:2.
ref_note: Take only the painting technique and the palette from it, not its composition or its objects.

prompt:
Turn the attached painting into a flat colour-coded segmentation map for an animation tool. Keep the composition, the outlines, the positions and the proportions of the attached image exactly, as if traced on a clear sheet laid on top of it: the same framing, the same horizon height, the same size and place of every object. Replace every area by one flat, pure, fully saturated colour with hard, clean edges: no shading, no texture, no brush strokes, no outlines, no gradients, no glow, no halos, no details inside the areas. It is a technical map, not a picture: do not keep any colour of the attached painting, use only the colour codes below.

Colour codes: the sky seen through the windows, including all clouds and stars, down to the horizon: pure blue #0000FF. The sea seen through the windows, from the horizon down to the window sill: pure cyan #00FFFF. The glowing glass lens of the big lighthouse lamp, with the brass lamp inside it: pure orange #FF8000. Everything else (the walls, the ceiling, the window frames and bars, the floor, the desk with everything on it, the iron staircase, the rope and the crate): pure black #000000. Use no other colours, and do not add, remove or move any object.

No text, letters, numbers, signatures, watermarks or logos anywhere in the image. No real places, brands, franchises or recognisable characters from existing games or films.

Image format: landscape 3:2.
